title: Finding Your People
blurb: The through-line of every survey: Vibecamp as the place people finally belong. What began as meeting Twitter mutuals became, year over year, a community people call home.

title: No Small Talk
blurb: Every year, people report the same astonishment: conversations go deep immediately. The shared context does the warmup, and small talk signals goodbye, not hello.
entries: Conversations You Can't Get Anywhere Else

title: You Can Just Do Things
blurb: From spontaneous blanket forts at VC1 to a full schedule of camper-run events, the lesson has been consistent: there is no program except the one campers make — and every year they make it better.

title: Coming Alone
blurb: "I didn't know anyone" is the most common way people arrive. The on-ramps that work are small and structured: a cabin crew, a tent village, a volunteer shift, a pre-party.
response: Coming solo? Join our Discord to find or form a cabin crew before camp, or volunteer to help with something (the teahouse always needs hands) — a job makes it much easier to make new friends!

title: The Newcomer Gap
blurb: The community's most persistent challenge. Named at VC2 as "the lemur problem," it has appeared in every survey since — the flip side of a community dense enough to feel like home.
response: We're brainstorming ways to help first-time attendees have a softer arrival at camp, but this is also clearly an activity gap! If you're not sure what to host at VC6, why not create a welcome event of some sort for newcomers?

title: The Gender Ratio
blurb: Vibecamp skewed heavily male early on, and women told us plainly what that was like. The mix is changing: women were 17% of VC2 respondents and 32% at VC5.
response: Women were 17% of VC2 respondents and 32% at VC5 — the trend is in the demographics section above.

title: Taking Care of Each Other
blurb: Physical safety is the highest-rated question every single year. Getting there took work, and the surveys show it: asks at VC2, fixes noticed at VC3, policies codified by VC5.
response: Safety now has a full, dedicated team of year-round volunteers — see the policies they've helped develop for us here.

title: Camping Is Camping
blurb: June in Maryland means heat, bugs, and a thin mattress. Veterans bring earplugs and a sleep mask, consider booking offsite lodging if they run hot or sleep light, and check for ticks.

title: The Teahouse
blurb: Beloved from day one, iterated to perfection by VC3, and now a victim of its own success. The teahouse's arc is the story of Vibecamp's growth in miniature.

title: MORE DAYS
blurb: The request that has outlived every other complaint: VC1 attendees begged in all caps for more days. Camp has grown longer since — and the ask persists, now with a consensus answer: one more day.
response: OKAY okay we heard you, new for VC6: optional add-on ticket now available for people who want to show up a day early : )

title: The Food Saga
blurb: From "widely panned" at VC1 to a hellish food tent at Vibeclipse to surprised praise (and a plea for earlier dinner) at VC5 — slow, real progress.
entries: Dinner at Seven Was a Crime

title: Schedules, Signage & Signal
blurb: The perennial operational gripe: finding out what's happening, where, without working wifi. Each year's tooling improves on the last; each year the ask continues.

title: The Vibes-to-Romance Pipeline
blurb: Present since the very first event, and operating at peak efficiency by VC4 — at least one attendee has reported meeting the person they plan to marry.

title: A Place to Become Yourself
blurb: Beyond the parties, people consistently describe Vibecamp as transformative — a safe container to experiment with identity and come back changed.
